actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The default MuJoCo configuration runs the scene g1_description/scene.xml
The scene includes the robot model g1_29dof_rev_1_0.xml
The robot model uses radians and resolves its meshes from meshes/
The robot model sets the integration step to 0.002 s and the implicit integrator
The robot model declares a free floating-base joint named floating_base_joint
The floating base starts at the pelvis body pose (0 0 0.793)
The actuator block has 29 motor elements, one for each actuated joint, and none states a ctrlrange
The left hip pitch joint has range -2.5307 to 2.8798 rad and actuatorfrcrange -88 to 88
The left ankle roll joint has range -0.2618 to 0.2618 rad and actuatorfrcrange -50 to 50
The left wrist pitch joint has range -1.61443 to 1.61443 rad and actuatorfrcrange -5 to 5
The simulation loop loads the scene with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path and creates the MjData
The simulation loop overrides the model timestep with cfg.simulation_dt
The configuration sets simulation_dt to 0.003 s and control_decimation to 7

The configuration's tau_limit array lists the per-actuator torque magnitudes: 88, 139 and 50 for the leg motors, 88, 50 and 50 for the waist, 25 for the shoulder and elbow motors and 5 for the wrist motors
The simulation loop clips the computed torque with np.clip(tau, -tau_limit, tau_limit) before writing it to d.ctrl
The simulation loop calls mujoco.mj_step once per iteration
The simulation loop treats qpos[7:] as the 29 joint positions and qvel[6:] as the 29 joint velocities, so the first seven qpos and six qvel values are the floating base
The simulation loop runs the FSM when sim_counter is a multiple of control_decimation
The README documents running the MuJoCo simulation with python deploy_mujoco/deploy_mujoco.py
The README documents the LieDown start model with the override xml_path=g1_description/g1_29dof_LieDown.xml

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from one initial state; cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults (mj_resetData plus mj_forward) and takes no seed parameter, so no seed selects a different state; this package's fake is a placeholder integrator and was not compared with MuJoCo

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses scene.xml and its include for the joint and actuator counts, the free-base start pose and the 2 ms model timestep, but integrates a placeholder torque response and resolves no mesh, texture, contact, constraint, gravity, inertia or sensor

MuJoCo was not installed and cannot be installed where the gate ran (no network, no pip), so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine; the sim path (a backend name backends does not list, which imports the real mujoco module) was not run

the upstream deploy_mujoco.py loop overrides the model timestep with simulation_dt 0.003 s, runs the FSM every 7 steps and reads a joystick (deploy_mujoco/deploy_mujoco.py:35, :57-90; deploy_mujoco/config/mujoco.yaml:3-4); this driver loads the scene directly, keeps the model's 0.002 s step and exposes data.ctrl, so it is not the upstream joystick and policy application
no policy, joystick, viewer or FSM is modelled; the package is a local MuJoCo world, not the upstream deploy_mujoco application and not a physical robot

the fake's free-base reset starts at the pelvis body pose (0 0 0.793) and identity quaternion; it does not run MuJoCo's qpos0 or forward kinematics, and its step does not clamp joints to their model ranges

the model's motors declare no ctrlrange, so the bridge publishes action.ctrl operator_required: a step that sets it is refused until the site's site-limits.json bounds it, and site-limits.example.json is operator example data, not a model bound; the upstream deploy_mujoco.py application clips tau to tau_limit (deploy_mujoco/config/mujoco.yaml:5-9, deploy_mujoco/deploy_mujoco.py:86-87), but this driver does not present that application clamp as a model bound

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

operator_required.name: step
operator_required.reason: the model gives none of its actuators no control range (ctrllimited false or no ctrlrange), so MuJoCo leaves the control unclamped; site-limits.json must bound action.ctrl before a step can set it

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
